pr_title: Suggest `each` when `map` or `collect` is used in void context
pr_body:
Using `map` in a void context can either be replaced with `map!` if mutation of the underlying object is desired, or with `each` when it is only being invoked for the side effects produced by a block passed in.

This PR updates the cop to suggest `each` in instead of `map!`.

Fixes https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/issues/8270
Fixes https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/issues/4305
Fixes https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/issues/1052

* [x] Added an entry (file) to the [changelog folder](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop/blob/master/changelog/) named `{change_type}_{change_description}.md` if the new code introduces user-observable changes. issue_context.title: Cop idea: prefer each over map when return value is not used
issue_context.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I found a code like this:

```ruby
Model.all.map { do_something_as_side_effect }
```

I think everyone will agree that we should use `each` instead of `map` in this case, since `map` is mainly used for its return value but here it's not used.

This sort of thing can be automated by RuboCop!

## Describe the solution you'd like

When a method named `map` is used and the return value is not used, the cop warns.
It can support auto-correct to replace `map` with `each`.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Actually, there are some more methods from `Enumerable` module that we use for their return values, such as `select`.
We might let users specify method names to replace with `each`

## Additional context
 
When a user defines their own method named `map`, this cop might produce false positive. However, when it's named as `map`, it clearly shows that it's expected to return value and we care it.
comments: Thanks I didn't notice this old issue.

@fatkodima Good catch!
This issue has been closed in the past. Opening as a PR would be welcome. See #1052 for more information. Thank you.

review_comments: `collect` feels more tenuous here; I'm happy to remove it and keep the cop suggesting `collect!` instead
`collect` is an alias for `map`, it should be consistent with the same behavior.

there are a few more candidates for this cop but maybe they are too niche.
like `reverse` vs `reverse_each` 

should we consider adding those?
IMHO, I remember seeing `map` used in code where `each` should have been used. OTOH, In my experience `reverse` doesn't look that familiar. So I think it can start with just `map` and `collect`.
